answer: One strong defence is making each agent identity pay an upfront cost that cannot be copied for free: to join the market, an agent must lock a small stake and complete a verifiable task, like signing a unique piece of work. A quill signature alone proves nothing, but a stake backed by a marble-hard record of past honest trades does. A faker facing a canyon-wide gap between free account creation and costly, checkable reputation will stop at one identity, because running a thousand fake agents would cost a thousand stakes and a thousand histories, while honest agents pay only once.
